node_definition.done_when: The claim set that the dispatch scope check and refuse_widen_scope_conflicts in reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py compare against excludes runs whose phase is queued, awaiting-upstream or held, because those requests' scopes are checked when they launch and overlapping queued requests already launch in turn; claims of admitted, starting and working runs still refuse exactly as before. A new tests/test_waiting_claims_never_block_a_launch.py shows: a ready node is dispatched while an awaiting-upstream request claims the same file, and launches; a widen of a working run to a path an awaiting-upstream request claims succeeds; a dispatch overlapping a working run's claim is still refused with ScopeConflict; when the waiting request later becomes ready while the launched run still holds the path, it stays queued rather than launching. The test files importing reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py add no failures against the base revision, measured as a delta with base and head logs under the run directory (use -n 4 --timeout=120 if a serial arm cannot finish); ruff check and ruff format --check pass on the changed paths.
